hero.heading:

problem.heading:
The asset is found.
Is it ready for the next job?
problem.intro: Location starts the decision. Add the event or condition that tells dispatch, the custodian or maintenance what to check next.

cards.title: Equipment is spread across sites
cards.body: A generator, trailer or reusable carrier can stay at a customer location after the job ends. Connect the reported site to the return plan and responsible contact.

cards.title: Available does not mean service-ready
cards.body: A map cannot show whether powered equipment needs attention or sensitive contents experienced unsuitable conditions. Add the measurement that informs the actual redeployment decision.

cards.title: An unexpected move or opening
cards.body: A transfer outside the agreed plan or an opened equipment case needs follow-up. Specify movement, door or tamper events around the asset, then verify them with the responsible site.

problem.takeaway: Combine the reported location with the evidence your team needs to release the asset for its next task.

focus.heading:
Make the next move
an informed one.
focus.intro: Use the asset identity to connect different records, while preserving when and where each observation was made.

stages.title: Locate & check age
stages.body: Read the latest available position with its observation time, receipt time and available validity information.

stages.title: Review relevant condition
stages.body: Add selected machine or case-environment records where they affect the next use. Compare readings under suitable operating conditions.

stages.title: Check service & custody
stages.body: Compare configured movement and any separately supplied opening events with the rental, service and site-handover records.

stages.title: Assign the next action
stages.body: Confirm collection, inspection or redeployment with the team that owns the decision.

focus.note: A location report cannot establish equipment serviceability. Additional sensor records and the required inspection inform that separate decision.
focus.detailTitle: Keep each observation in its proper context
focus.detail: A parked asset may report position less often than one in transfer. Vibration measurements on powered equipment need a defined mounting point and comparable speed or load; transport movement is a different measurement task. A case logger measures its local air, not every stored item. Link records through the asset ID, keep observation timestamps and identify stale or missing data before presenting an operational status.

applications.heading:
One asset record.
Different operating decisions.
applications.intro: Start with what the team needs to locate, collect or return to service. Add supporting measurements around that decision.

measurements.heading:
Each field should support
an asset decision.
measurements.intro: Select the record around collection, condition review or service planning—not the number of available channels.

rows.measure: Position, positioning method and observation time
rows.decision: Which site should the collection team contact?
rows.selection: Specified positioning, antenna exposure, network support and update profile.

rows.measure: Movement or geofence event with supporting history
rows.selection: Event logic, reporting gaps, site geometry and named recipient.

rows.measure: Separately supplied door, light or tamper input
rows.decision: Does an opening or possible device removal need a custody check?
rows.selection: Sensor type, fixing, permitted access periods, compatible input and event notification path.

rows.measure: Separate machine vibration / temperature at defined operating states
rows.decision: Does maintenance need to inspect before redeployment?
rows.selection: Sensor placement, measured quantity and comparable speed / load; machine run-time from a suitable independent input.

rows.measure: Separate local temperature and humidity history
rows.decision: Does the stored equipment or cargo need exposure review?
rows.selection: Sensing position, recording duration and planned retrieval.

rows.measure: Supplied tracker power status, machine operating hours and maintenance records
rows.decision: What must be serviced or verified before the next job?
rows.selection: Confirm each payload field; tracker battery is not machine battery condition, and movement time is not engine run-time.

measurements.boundary: Tracking and condition review support operational decisions. Required equipment inspections, machine protection and personnel safety remain with the appropriate systems and procedures.

platform.heading:
Hitelecom Cloud.
An asset record with context.
platform.intro: Scope location, selected condition views and service references around the asset ID. Integrate the agreed fields with your existing fleet or maintenance system where required.
platform.insight: Check position age alongside the service and condition records needed for collection. The site contact confirms physical availability.

steps.title: Dispatch
steps.body: Check the reported site and data age; review configured transfer events before assigning collection.

steps.title: Maintenance
steps.body: Review selected condition history with service records and complete the required inspection.

steps.title: Site or pool manager
steps.body: Check any reported opening or tamper event, confirm custody and access, then record the handover.

platform.boundary: Combined views require agreed fields and interfaces. A tracker does not provide automatic immobilisation, personnel rescue or equipment protection.

faq.q: Which sensors are useful beyond the asset tracker?
faq.a: Choose the addition around a decision. Separate machine vibration or temperature can focus maintenance checks. Door or tamper sensing can prompt a custody check. Local temperature and humidity recording can document a sensitive case environment. Actual run-time may come from an approved machine interface. These additions need confirmed hardware and data paths; they are not built-in channels in every tracker.

faq.q: Is the displayed position the asset’s current location?
faq.a: It is the latest position available to the platform. Show its observation time and receipt time because they can differ. Compare the age with the expected reporting schedule. If the position is stale or uncertain, confirm the asset with the responsible site before dispatching a collection.

faq.q: How do we choose H300 4G or H500 NB-IoT?
faq.a: Choose around actual sites and routes, the required update profile and operator support. Confirm bands, SIM service and any roaming requirement. Test mounting and reception on representative assets. Additional sensor data may use a different connection or local retrieval workflow; it is not automatically carried by the tracker.

faq.q: Can one vibration sensor measure machine condition and transport impacts?
faq.a: Not by assumption. The published machine sensor measures vibration velocity RMS within its specified frequency band. Transport shock recording needs suitable event capture, range and mounting. Define the quantity and operating context first, then select the instrument that supplies the evidence required for that task.

faq.q: Are door, tamper and shock functions included in H300 / H500?
faq.a: Do not assume this from the tracker name. Confirm the supplied hardware, inputs, event logic and platform fields. Door contacts, removal detection and shock recording may need separate devices or a project-specific design. Specify what constitutes an event, who receives it and how it is checked. An opening or light change does not by itself prove theft.

faq.q: Can motion or tracker battery data tell us machine operating hours?
faq.a: Movement is not the same as engine or pump operation. Use a documented run-status, machine telemetry or another validated input for operating hours. Tracker power status describes the tracker; equipment battery voltage or state of charge needs its own suitable measurement or BMS interface. Keep these fields separate so maintenance is scheduled from the correct evidence.

faq.q: Does a location or condition alert prove theft or unsafe equipment?
faq.a: No. An event identifies something for the responsible team to check. Confirm site transfers and authorised openings, inspect the equipment and review supporting records under the agreed procedure. No remote immobilisation, machine protection or personnel safety function is implied by this tracking page.

faq.q: How does this differ from the Smart Logistics solution?
faq.a: Asset tracking focuses on reusable equipment and carriers: location, custody, maintenance and the next deployment. Smart Logistics focuses on what a particular shipment experienced and its receiving decision. They can share IDs and selected observations while keeping equipment readiness and cargo acceptance as separate workflows.

faq.q: Can all records appear in our existing asset platform?
faq.a: A combined view can be scoped around supported interfaces. Agree asset IDs, units, observation and receipt timestamps, available health fields and access controls. Local logger exports need a separate retrieval and import process. Test delayed, missing and duplicate records before relying on a combined operational status.

architecture.heading:
Location leads.
Condition adds context.
architecture.intro: Build an asset-specific monitoring package. Tracking remains the core; additional sensors are selected only when they change maintenance, storage or deployment decisions.
